questions.question_text:
The graph of $y = \cos(2x)$ and the line $y = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ are shown for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-0.3, xmax=6.9, ymin=-1.6, ymax=1.6,
  xtick={1.5708, 3.1416, 4.7124, 6.2832},
  xticklabels={$\frac{\pi}{2}$, $\pi$, $\frac{3\pi}{2}$, $2\pi$},
  ytick={-1, 1},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=11cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=0:6.2832] {cos(deg(2*x))};
\addplot[thick, red, domain=0:6.2832] {0.86603};
\node[red, anchor=west] at (axis cs:6.45,0.86603) {$y=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
How many solutions does $\cos(2x) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ have for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$?

options.why: Counted only the first cycle instead of the two cycles the domain holds.
Multiplied the two crossings per cycle by the dilation constant $2$ as well as by the number of cycles.
Used a period of $\frac{2\pi}{3}$ instead of $\pi$, so counted three cycles.

questions.solution_text:
Period $=\dfrac{2\pi}{2}$
$=\pi$
The domain $0 \le x \le 2\pi$ holds two complete cycles.
The line $y=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ lies between $-1$ and $1$, so it cuts each cycle twice.
$2 \times 2 = 4$ points of intersection

questions.question_text:
The graph of $y = 5\sin(3x)$ and the line $y = 5$ are shown for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-0.3, xmax=6.9, ymin=-6.4, ymax=6.4,
  xtick={1.5708, 3.1416, 4.7124, 6.2832},
  xticklabels={$\frac{\pi}{2}$, $\pi$, $\frac{3\pi}{2}$, $2\pi$},
  ytick={-5, 5},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=11cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=0:6.2832] {5*sin(deg(3*x))};
\addplot[thick, red, domain=0:6.2832] {5};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
How many solutions does $5\sin(3x) = 5$ have for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$?

options.why: Assumed two crossings in each of the three cycles, missing that the line sits at the maximum.
Counted only the first cycle instead of the three cycles the domain holds.
Treated $y=5$ as lying outside the range of the curve rather than equal to its maximum.

questions.solution_text:
Period $=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$, so the domain holds three complete cycles.
The line $y=5$ sits at the maximum value of the curve, so it touches each cycle once instead of crossing it twice.
There are $3$ solutions.

questions.question_text:
The graph of $y = 6\cos x$ and the line $y = 2$ are shown for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-0.3, xmax=6.9, ymin=-7.5, ymax=7.5,
  xtick={1.5708, 3.1416, 4.7124, 6.2832},
  xticklabels={$\frac{\pi}{2}$, $\pi$, $\frac{3\pi}{2}$, $2\pi$},
  ytick={-6, 2, 6},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=11cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=0:6.2832] {6*cos(deg(x))};
\addplot[thick, red, domain=0:6.2832] {2};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
One solution of $6\cos x = 2$ is $x \approx 1.23$.
What is the other solution in $0 \le x \le 2\pi$, correct to two decimal places?

options.why: Used $\pi - 1.23$, which is the symmetry of a sine curve about $x=\frac{\pi}{2}$, not a cosine curve.
Added $\pi$ to the known solution, treating the half-period as the gap between solutions.
Added the period $2\pi$ to the known solution, which lands outside the given domain.

questions.solution_text:
The two intersections lie either side of the minimum at $x=\pi$, so they are symmetric about it.
$x = 2\pi - 1.23$
$= 5.05$

questions.question_text:
The graph of $y = 3\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{5}\right)$ and the line $y = 3$ are shown for $0 \le x \le 30$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-1.2, xmax=32.5, ymin=-4, ymax=4,
  xtick={5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30},
  ytick={-3, 3},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=12cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=0:30] {3*sin(deg(pi*x/5))};
\addplot[thick, red, domain=0:30] {3};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
The curve has period $10$, and $x=2.5$ is a solution of $3\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{5}\right)=3$.
What are all the solutions in $0 \le x \le 30$?

options.why: Kept adding the period without checking that $32.5$ lies outside the domain.
Added half the period each time, as though the line crossed the curve twice per cycle.
Gave only the solution supplied, without using the period to reach the later cycles.

questions.solution_text:
The line sits at the maximum value of the curve, so it touches each cycle exactly once.
Each later touching point is one period further on.
$2.5 + 10 = 12.5$
$12.5 + 10 = 22.5$
The next value, $32.5$, lies outside the domain.
$x = 2.5,\ 12.5,\ 22.5$

questions.question_text:
The curve $y = \sin x$ and the line $y = \dfrac{x}{3}$ are shown.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-4.6, xmax=4.6, ymin=-1.8, ymax=1.8,
  xtick={-3.1416, 3.1416},
  xticklabels={$-\pi$, $\pi$},
  ytick={-1, 1},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=11cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=-4:4] {sin(deg(x))};
\addplot[thick, red, domain=-4:4] {x/3};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
How many solutions does $\sin x = \dfrac{x}{3}$ have over all real values of $x$?

options.why: Missed the intersection at the origin, where both graphs pass through $(0,0)$.
Counted only the crossing at the origin and ignored the two symmetric crossings either side.
Assumed the line meets every arch of the sine curve, ignoring that $|\frac{x}{3}|>1$ once $|x|>3$.

questions.solution_text:
Since $-1 \le \sin x \le 1$, a solution needs $\left|\dfrac{x}{3}\right| \le 1$.
$-3 \le x \le 3$
Inside this interval the graphs cross at the origin, once more for positive $x$ and once more for negative $x$.
The graphs meet $3$ times in total.

questions.question_text:
The curve $y = 5\sin x$ and the line $y = x+2$ are shown.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-9, xmax=5, ymin=-7, ymax=7,
  xtick={-6, -3, 3},
  ytick={-5, 5},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=12cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=-8:4] {5*sin(deg(x))};
\addplot[thick, red, domain=-8:4] {x+2};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Every solution of $5\sin x = x+2$ must lie in which interval?

options.why: Added $2$ to each end of $-5 \le x+2 \le 5$ instead of subtracting it.
Used the range of $5\sin x$ as the interval for $x$, ignoring the $+2$ in the line.
Used the range of $\sin x$ rather than $5\sin x$, and also ignored the $+2$.

questions.solution_text:
Since $-1 \le \sin x \le 1$:
$-5 \le 5\sin x \le 5$
At a solution, $x+2$ equals $5\sin x$.
$-5 \le x+2 \le 5$
$-7 \le x \le 3$

questions.question_text:
The graph of $y = 2\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)+1$ and the line $y = 2$ are shown for $0 \le x \le 8\pi$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-1.2, xmax=27, ymin=-2, ymax=4,
  xtick={6.2832, 12.5664, 18.8496, 25.1327},
  xticklabels={$2\pi$, $4\pi$, $6\pi$, $8\pi$},
  ytick={-1, 1, 2, 3},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=12cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=0:25.1327] {2*cos(deg(x/2))+1};
\addplot[thick, red, domain=0:25.1327] {2};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Solve $2\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)+1 = 2$ for $0 \le x \le 8\pi$.

options.why: Solved only the first revolution of $u=\frac{x}{2}$ instead of the full domain $0 \le u \le 4\pi$.
Found the four values of $u$ but never doubled them to recover $x$.
Doubled the values of $u$ twice, multiplying each solution by $4$ instead of by $2$.

questions.solution_text:
$2\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)+1 = 2$
$\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$
Let $u = \dfrac{x}{2}$, so $0 \le u \le 4\pi$.
$u = \dfrac{\pi}{3},\ \dfrac{5\pi}{3}$
Adding $2\pi$ to each gives two more values inside $0 \le u \le 4\pi$.
$u = \dfrac{\pi}{3},\ \dfrac{5\pi}{3},\ \dfrac{7\pi}{3},\ \dfrac{11\pi}{3}$
$x = 2u$
$x = \dfrac{2\pi}{3},\ \dfrac{10\pi}{3},\ \dfrac{14\pi}{3},\ \dfrac{22\pi}{3}$

questions.question_text:
The graph of $f(x) = 7\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{8}\right)+2$ and the line $y = 4$ are shown for $0 \le x \le 16$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-1, xmax=18.5, ymin=-6.5, ymax=11,
  xtick={4, 8, 12, 16},
  ytick={-5, 2, 4, 9},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=12cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=0:16] {7*cos(deg(pi*x/8))+2};
\addplot[thick, red, domain=0:16] {4};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
The function has period $16$ and a minimum at $x=8$.
Given that $x \approx 3.26$ is a solution of $f(x)=4$, what is the other solution in $0 \le x \le 16$, correct to two decimal places?

options.why: Added the known solution to the minimum's position instead of reflecting it in that position.
Subtracted the known solution from the minimum's position rather than from twice that position.
Added the period $16$ to the known solution, which lands outside the given domain.

questions.solution_text:
The two intersections lie either side of the minimum at $x=8$, so they are symmetric about it.
$x = 2(8) - 3.26$
$= 12.74$
